intent: Build a URL shortener service that creates short links from long URLs, redirects short codes to the original URLs, returns link details, and tracks per-link click analytics.

functional_needs.statement: A client can submit a long URL and receive a newly created short link (short code) for it.
functional_needs.source_quote: Create a short link from a long URL

functional_needs.statement: Requesting a short code redirects the client to the original long URL.
functional_needs.source_quote: redirect from the short code to the original URL

functional_needs.statement: The redirect uses HTTP status 302 (temporary redirect), so every click reaches the service and is counted.
functional_needs.source_quote: Use a temporary redirect (302) so every click reaches the service and is counted.

functional_needs.statement: A client can retrieve the details of an existing short link.
The service keeps a total click count for each short link, incremented on each redirect.
functional_needs.source_quote: Total click count per short link

functional_needs.statement: The service records the timestamp of the most recent click for each short link.
functional_needs.source_quote: plus the timestamp of the last click

functional_needs.statement: A client can retrieve a short link's analytics (total clicks and last-click timestamp) through an API call for that link.
functional_needs.source_quote: exposed via an API call for that link

nfr_asks.text: 'Reliability features' was requested without specifics. Clarification C-1 answered 'none', so no catalog NFR is added until the user picks one or more catalog entries.

ambiguities.question: Should a client be able to choose a custom alias for the short code, or are short codes always generated by the service?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Custom aliases change the create request, and they add conflict handling (for example, an alias that is already taken).
ambiguities.recommended_default: Short codes are always generated by the service; custom aliases are not supported.
options: Optional custom alias, rejected with a conflict error if already taken

ambiguities.question: When the same long URL is submitted more than once, should the service create a new short link each time or return the existing one?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: This decides whether click counts are shared or kept separate for repeat submissions, and what the create call returns.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Create a new, independent short link on each submission.
options: Always create a new short link
Return the existing short link for an identical long URL

ambiguities.question: Which long URLs are accepted when creating a short link?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: This decides which create requests are rejected and what error the client receives.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Accept only absolute http/https URLs and reject anything else with a client error.

ambiguities.question: What fields make up a short link's details, and are the analytics returned in the details call or by a separate call?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: This determines the shape of the details and analytics responses.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Details include the short code, the original URL and the creation timestamp; analytics (total clicks and last-click timestamp) are returned by a separate per-link call.
options: Analytics included in the details response
Both: analytics in the details response and also via a separate call

ambiguities.question: What should the redirect, details and analytics calls return for a short code that does not exist?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: This defines the error behavior clients will observe.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Return 404 Not Found for unknown short codes on all three calls.
options: 410 Gone for codes that once existed, 404 otherwise

ambiguities.question: What should the last-click timestamp be for a link that has never been clicked?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: This affects the analytics response for new links.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Click count of 0 and a null/absent last-click timestamp.

ambiguities.question: Should every redirect count as a click, including repeat clicks from the same client?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: This affects the reported click totals.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Count every successful redirect as one click, with no de-duplication or bot filtering.

ambiguities.question: Do creating links or viewing details and analytics require authentication or link ownership?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Access control changes who can call each operation.
ambiguities.recommended_default: No authentication; all operations are public.
options: Authentication required to create links and view analytics

out_of_scope: Rate limiting, contract input validation and Prometheus metrics NFRs (C-1 answered 'none')
Uptime, failover and durability guarantees (cannot be built or validated per C-1)
Updating or deleting short links (not requested)
Per-click analytics beyond total count and last-click timestamp, such as referrer, geography or user agent (not requested)
